references.text: God announces for the first time that he will send a flood to destroy all life on earth – the background to the warning in 7:4.
The fulfillment of God's word in 7:4: rain fell over the earth for forty days and forty nights.
The Lord reigned over the flood – a reference to God's sovereign rule over the flood in Noah's time.
By faith Noah, being warned about what had not yet been seen, built an ark in reverence to save his family. The verse refers to God's warning and Noah's obedient response.
Peter notes that God did not spare the ancient world but preserved Noah and seven others when he brought the flood upon the ungodly.
Peter refers to how the world of that time was destroyed when it was flooded with water – an example of God's judgment.
Jesus compares his return to the days of Noah: people lived as usual until the flood came and took them all away.
6:7 reveals the theological reason (God's regret) behind the judgment warned in 7:4.
Zephaniah uses the flood judgment as a theological pattern for the final judgment on ungodliness.
Zephaniah 1:2 alludes to the flood judgment as an example of God's power to completely destroy.
7:10 marks the beginning of the flood after the seven-day period in 7:4 has expired.
